headline: Heard a BFFA grievance asking that pension changes negotiated for BPOA be extended to firefighters.
summary: The firefighters' union argued that police pension changes, including counting 10% of overtime toward final pay, should apply to firefighters automatically. The city said the grievance was untimely and that the police changes should not be applied identically without weighing overall actuarial impact. Commissioners then went into executive session to discuss matters where public knowledge would put the department at a substantial disadvantage.
plain_text:
Burlington Fire Commission Meeting  
Tuesday October 30, 2026 08:00-09:41 
Members Present: Chair Jake Perskinson, Vice Chair Kevin McLaughlin, Monica Chapman, and 
Ashley Bond. Chief Michael Curtin, BFFA Union President Joshua Kirtlink, BFFA Union 
Secretary Philip Edgerley, BFFA Attorney James Hykel, City Attorney Hayley McClenahan, 
CAO Katherine Schad, Director of Finance Bradley Kukenberger, HR Director Lynn Reagan, 
Council for the Commission Anthony Larrapino, and Administrative Assistant Meghan 
Sweeney.  
Call to Order –  
The meeting called to order October 30, 2026 at 08:00 am. 
 
Grievance Presentation-  
Meeting summary generated by AI 
 The Fire Commission heard a grievance from the BFFA arguing that pension 
enhancements negotiated for BPOA—especially counting 10% of overtime toward 
average final compensation and allowing purchase of prior service credit—should 
automatically extend to firefighters under the fire contract’s pension-equity language.  
 The City argued the grievance was untimely, that the fire-police pension equity ratio 
remained intact, and that the BPOA changes were bargained-for provisions whose value 
should not be automatically or identically applied to BFFA without considering overall 
actuarial impact.  
 Commissioners asked clarifying questions about notice, timeliness, the meaning of 
“value,” whether financial impact should matter, and how the disputed contract 
provisions should be interpreted before moving toward deliberation.  
  
Executive Session –  
 Pursuant to Title 1, Section 313 of the Vermont Statues, upon the affirmative vote a majority of 
the members present, a motion to go into executive session is carried to discuss matters where 
general public knowledge would place the Department at a substantial disadvantage. Motion to 
go into executive session by Commission McLaughlin and seconded by Commissioner 
Chapman. Meeting went into executive session at 09:17 and all others left the meeting. 
 
Adjournment-  
Motion to adjourn made by Commissioner McLaughlin and seconded by Commissioner 
Chapman at 09:41.
